questions.text: A user issues a Linux command and the result is shown. Which Linux command is used to display the contents of the current directory as shown?
questions.context:
total 40
drwxr-xr-x 2 devasc devasc 4096 Apr 15 19:09 Videos
drwxr-xr-x 2 devasc devasc 4096 Apr 15 19:09 Templates
drwxr-xr-x 5 devasc devasc 4096 Mar 30 21:24 snap
drwxr-xr-x 2 devasc devasc 4096 Apr 15 19:09 Public
drwxr-xr-x 2 devasc devasc 4096 Apr 15 19:09 Pictures
drwxr-xr-x 2 devasc devasc 4096 Apr 15 19:09 Music
drwxr-xr-x 5 devasc devasc 4096 Mar 30 21:21 labs
drwxr-xr-x 2 devasc devasc 4096 Apr 15 19:09 Downloads
drwxr-xr-x 2 devasc devasc 4096 Apr 15 19:09 Documents
drwxr-xr-x 2 devasc devasc 4096 Mar 30 21:25 Desktop
devasc@labvm:~$
questions.explanation: The long format (permissions, owner, size, date) means -l, and the names run in reverse alphabetical order (Videos first, Desktop last), which is -r. So it's ls -lr. Plain ls -l would list Desktop first. -a would also show hidden dotfiles, and ln creates links rather than listing anything.

questions.text: A program executes a division operation inside a try block that triggers a ZeroDivisionError. The exception is caught by an except ZeroDivisionError: block, followed by a finally: block. Under what condition does the code inside the finally: block execute?
options: Only if no exception occurs in the try block.
Only if the exception is caught by an except block.
Only when the program exits without errors.
Regardless of whether an exception occurred or was handled.
questions.explanation: finally always runs once the try/except finishes: with or without an exception, and whether or not it was caught. That's why it's used for cleanup.

questions.text: A system administrator is preparing a Linux server for maintenance and decides to execute the apt-get upgrade command in the terminal. What is the specific action that the apt-get upgrade command performs in this scenario?
options: Operating system updates are downloaded and will be installed.
Operating system updates are downloaded and will be installed.
Every application installed on the system will update itself to the latest version.
The remote repository of applications and dependencies will be updated to the latest version.
questions.warning: This is the keyed answer, though strictly speaking the apps don't update themselves: apt upgrades every installed package (operating system packages included) to the latest version in the repositories.
questions.explanation: apt-get upgrade upgrades every installed application/package to its latest available version, which is what this option describes. "Operating system updates are downloaded and will be installed" is too narrow, since it upgrades all installed packages, not just the OS. Refreshing the repository package lists is apt-get update, and "upgrade" is a subcommand, not a package name.

questions.text: A script reads data line-by-line from a text file using with open("config.txt", "r") as file:. Using the with context manager guarantees that the file is automatically closed upon exiting the block, even if an error occurs while reading.
questions.explanation: Leaving a with block always calls the file's close, whether the block ends normally or because an exception was raised, so you don't need an explicit file.close().
